column1: # clues.tsv for ft_strchr -- pedagogic hints only. NEVER state the expected value or the fix.
# Format: <hint><TAB><CASE label><TAB>...   (fires if ANY listed case fails)
# The contract is man 3 strchr (Libft, p.8: "adhering strictly to their definitions in the man page").
strchr returns a pointer to the FIRST occurrence of c. What does it return when c is not in the string at all (man 3 strchr, RETURN VALUE)?
The man page says the terminating null byte is "considered part of the string". So when c is 0, is there an occurrence to find, and where is it?
c is an int and the string holds chars: is a plain char signed on this machine? When the byte is 0xe9 and c is 233, are the two values you compare equal? Which conversion makes them so?
Right on short strings, wrong on a long one? Which types does your position pass through, and can each of them reach 4999?
